text:
<!--
  THE AGENT'S JOB DESCRIPTION — editable capability text, same as prompt.md.

  Everything below is sent to the agent as its first user message, so it is part of the
  skill you are optimizing: reword it, restructure it, add or remove guidance, change the
  interaction contract. This comment block is STRIPPED before the agent sees it.

  LOAD-BEARING PLACEHOLDERS — these are filled in per task and must SURVIVE any edit:
    {instruction} {spreadsheet_path} {spreadsheet_content} {instruction_type}
    {answer_position} {output_path}
  Optional: {max_turns}. No other {braces} are allowed.

  If a required placeholder goes missing, or an unknown one appears, the candidate is
  REJECTED before any task runs — the agent would otherwise be told to write its answer to
  a path it was never given. A literal brace must be doubled: {{ or }}.
-->
You need to solve the following spreadsheet manipulation question. It contains six pieces of information:
- instruction: the question about spreadsheet manipulation.
- spreadsheet_path: the path of the spreadsheet file you need to manipulate.
- spreadsheet_content: the first few rows of the content of the spreadsheet file.
- instruction_type: Cell-Level Manipulation (answer_position is exact cell(s)) or Sheet-Level Manipulation (answer_position is the maximum range you may modify).
- answer_position: the cell(s)/range you must modify or fill in.
- output_path: write the modified spreadsheet file to this exact path.

### instruction
{instruction}

### spreadsheet_path
{spreadsheet_path}

### spreadsheet_content
{spreadsheet_content}

### instruction_type
{instruction_type}

### answer_position
{answer_position}

### output_path
{output_path}

Remember: your solution code will be re-run on other, differently-sized copies of this
spreadsheet, so it must COMPUTE the answer from the file's actual data (detect the real
last row/column) — never hardcode values, a fixed row range, or a copied sample sheet.

You have up to {max_turns} rounds of interaction. In each round, reply with exactly ONE python code block:
1. Information-gathering code (e.g. inspecting the file) — the execution result is returned to you.
2. Solution code that writes the modified file to output_path.
3. Verification code: re-open output_path (openpyxl, data_only=False) and, for answer_position,
   print and CHECK each of the following before you finish. If any check fails, fix your code and write again:
   - The VALUE and Python TYPE of each cell. Confirm the type matches the answer's nature (a real
     date/number for a converted date/number; text for text you split or copied out — a split-out
     piece stays text even if it looks like a date). If a cell holds a formula string, it is fine
     ONLY if it recalculates correctly: ordinary scalar formulas (SUM, SUMIF, INDEX/MATCH, VLOOKUP,
     WORKDAY, numeric SUMPRODUCT) and legacy Ctrl-Shift-Enter array formulas (SMALL(IF(...)), array
     INDEX/MATCH) are fine and should be kept; but a modern spill / dynamic-array function (FILTER,
     SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE, TEXTSPLIT, anything with an `_xlfn.` prefix), a volatile function
     (RANDBETWEEN, NOW, TODAY), a blank-test with `<>""`/`=""`, or a formula returning TRUE/FALSE
     will NOT recalculate correctly — recompute the value in Python and rewrite the literal.
   - The COUNT of filled cells versus the size of the range, counting what each formula EVALUATES
     to (not the formula string): a formula whose branch returns "" leaves that cell EMPTY after
     recalculation, so it does not count as filled. When the instruction fills a column/block, every
     applicable cell must hold a real value; a shortfall means you assumed the data ended too early,
     a lookup silently failed, or an IF branch returned "" — fix and rewrite.
   - That you did not intentionally write VALUES into cells OUTSIDE answer_position. Compare cell
     VALUES, not openpyxl's internal representation: re-saving a workbook can harmlessly re-serialize
     untouched formula cells without changing their values, and that is fine — do NOT treat it as a
     violation. Never hand-edit the .xlsx XML or repackage its zip to force this check to pass; that
     can corrupt the file so the grader cannot recalculate it. Always write with a normal openpyxl save.
Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct.
If your code raises an error, the traceback will be returned to you; fix the code and try again.
